rows.description: A teenager walking while texting fails to notice a cyclist or a pit. Looking is not seeing when attention is elsewhere.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 4–6, 7–12, 18–22, 23–26

rows.description: A young driver on a call or app misses a pedestrian in plain view. It is not carelessness of character but a limit of attention that habit and rules must guard against.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 4–6, 7–12, 13–17, 23–26

rows.description: A wise worker puts the phone away for driving, safety checks and key conversations, and double-checks critical work with a second person.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 4–6, 7–12, 13–17, 18–22

rows.description: A child doing homework with a cartoon on believes he is doing both well. He is switching quickly and doing each worse and more slowly.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 13–17, 18–22, 23–26

rows.description: A teenager replies to messages while studying and feels productive, but each switch costs focus and he needs time to get back into the topic.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 7–12, 18–22, 23–26

rows.description: A student with tabs, chat and lecture open thinks he can follow all, but notes and memory suffer. Rapid switching feels efficient and is not.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 7–12, 13–17, 23–26

rows.description: A productive professional works in single-task blocks, silences notifications, and batches messages, then rests. Fewer switches means better work in less time.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 7–12, 13–17, 18–22

rows.description: A team lead sees colleagues half-listening while typing, and sets a norm of full attention for short meetings instead of long distracted ones.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 7–12, 13–17, 18–22

rows.description: A preschooler tells about a past event and adds details from stories or what he was told. Each retelling reshapes the memory to fit what he understands.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 7–12, 13–17, 18–22, 23–26

rows.description: A child recounts a family trip with new bits copied from siblings' versions and believes them fully. Memory is rebuilt at each recall, not played back like a video.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 4–6, 13–17, 18–22, 23–26
